hypotheses.paper: tachyon: 'a hyperbolic action of Γ = ℤ on θ'
hypotheses.note: every x₀, every spacelike v, every g ∈ Isom₀ ∖ {1} fixing x₀ + ℝv pointwise (proved to be a boost, eq_boostAff_of_fix), every m ≠ 0; g acts on P = v^⊥ by a hyperbolic A (IsHyperbolicPlaneMap)

hypotheses.paper: photon: 'a parabolic action of Γ = ℤ on θ'
hypotheses.note: every x₀, every non-zero null v, every g ∈ Isom₀ ∖ {1} fixing x₀ + ℝv pointwise (proved to be a null rotation, eq_parabAff_of_fix), every m ≠ 0; g acts on P ≅ E^{1,2}/ℝv by a parabolic A (IsParabolicPlaneMap), ℝv-component κ

hypotheses.paper: 'action of Γ = ℤ on the coordinate θ', 'with the identification D_∞ = ℝ₊* × \widetilde{RP¹} ∪ {(0,0)}', 'variations of the above example'
hypotheses.note: Γ = GammaA (2π) acts on θ ALONE ((r,θ,z) ↦ (r,θ+2π,z), r and z fixed), as the Γ_α of the example; the identification of θ with \widetilde{RP¹} is a homeomorphism ψ : ℝ ≃ₜ ℝ conjugating the generator to the lift rayAngleLift A m : θ ↦ θ + rayShift A θ + 2πm of the action of A on the rays of P (ThetaLiftQuotient.lift), so the action on θ is the hyperbolic (parabolic) one; the developing map sends (r,θ,z) to the ray of angle ψθ (ThetaLiftQuotient.dev_eq). The first-dispatched Euclidean-radius reading (rayLiftHomeo, rescaling r) is NOT this and its quotient is not Hausdorff (findings).

hypotheses.paper: l.668 / def l.474: the quotient 'is naturally a singular (G,X)-manifold' (Hausdorff, second countable, locally connected, maximal a.e. structure)
hypotheses.note: ThetaLiftQuotient: T2Space, SecondCountableTopology, LocallyConnectedSpace of Γ\(D_∞ × ℝ), homeomorphic to ℂ × ℝ, IsProperlyDiscontinuous in FULL (both halves, via IsProperlyDiscontinuous.of_t2Space_orbits), free on {r>0}, unique maximal a.e. (Isom₀, E^{1,2})-structure making the projection an a.e. morphism, sing ⊆ π{r=0}

hypotheses.paper: (previous round) 'the action is free and properly discontinuous' for the Euclidean-radius lift
hypotheses.note: RayLiftQuotient.disc (and IsTurning.disc, homeoZ_quotient) is only the NEIGHBOURHOOD half of IsProperlyDiscontinuous; orbit separation fails at the axis for that action (tachyon: off-axis orbits accumulate at axis points; photon: distinct axis points are inseparable) — proved: rayLiftQuotient_tachyon_not_t1, rayLiftQuotient_photon_not_t2. These decls are kept, documented as the defect record, and no longer appear in the headline statements.

findings: l.682 holds as written, read literally: with Γ = ℤ acting on θ alone (r and z fixed), as a variation of the action Γ_α of the example, and θ identified with \widetilde{RP¹} by a homeomorphism ψ conjugating the generator to the lift of A, the quotient is a singular (Isom₀, E^{1,2})-manifold (Hausdorff, locally connected, second countable, ≅ ℂ × ℝ) with holonomy g (tachyon_isom0, photon_isom0, ThetaLiftQuotient). The developing map is then not Euclidean-polar in θ: D(r,θ,z) = x₀ + (z + r b(θ)) c v + r R(θ) w(e^{iψθ}), R > 0, built from a fundamental-domain curve extended equivariantly.

Feed-back to BBS (papers/bbs/REVIEW.md §H.2, POSTWAVE5/BBS-NOTES.md (3)): the construction there — 1·(r,θ,z) = (r‖g w(θ)‖/‖w(ĝθ+2πm)‖, ĝθ+2πm, z) with w a 2π-periodic Euclidean parametrisation — does not give a Hausdorff quotient, because the action rescales the Euclidean radius while 𝔻_∞'s apex neighbourhoods are {r < ε}: for the tachyon the quotient is not even T₁ (a point of the contracted eigen-ray lies in every neighbourhood of an axis point, GX.rayLiftQuotient_tachyon_not_t1, every β ≠ 0, every m), for the photon it is not T₂ (p_n = (−1/(s²n²), 1/(sn), 0) → (apex, 0) while φⁿp_n = (−1/(s²n²), 0, 1) → (apex, 1), GX.rayLiftQuotient_photon_not_t2, every s ≠ 0, every m). §H.2 checks only the neighbourhood half (hdisc) of proper discontinuity, which holds. The fix is to make the action preserve r: choose w equivariant (w(ĝθ + 2πm) = g w(θ), defined on a fundamental domain and extended), equivalently act on θ alone.

For the photon no complement of ℝv is invariant under a null rotation, so in the Euclidean-radius reading the action must also shift z ((r,θ,z) ↦ (r‖Ae^{iθ}‖, θ + rayShift A θ + 2πm, z + r κ(e^{iθ}))); BBS H.2's z-preserving formula holds only for the tachyon. In the corrected reading the drift is absorbed in the developing map (the term r b(θ) c v).

Every element of Isom₀ fixing a spacelike (resp. null) line pointwise is a boost (resp. a null rotation): the orientation-reversing candidates (exchange of the two null lines of v^⊥; γ = −1 for the null case) are excluded only by the determinant condition of Isom₀.

l.682 names no lift of the PSL(2,ℝ) element to \widetilde{RP¹}: the lift is a choice m ∈ ℤ of sheets. Every m ≠ 0 is certified (m = ±1 the tachyon/photon proper); m = 0 (the lift fixing the eigen-rays) is not claimed.
questions: 'Tachyon' / 'photon' are undefined in the paper; read as the variations whose holonomy is g ∈ Isom₀ ∖ {1} fixing pointwise a spacelike (resp. null) line (the literature's meaning, Particules_1, barbot2012particles). 'A hyperbolic (resp. parabolic) action of Γ = ℤ on θ with the identification D_∞ = ℝ₊* × \widetilde{RP¹} ∪ {(0,0)}' is read literally: Γ acts on θ alone and the identification ψ conjugates it to the lift of A. If the author meant instead the Euclidean-radius action (θ the Euclidean angle of P, r its Euclidean radius), that reading is false (the quotient is not Hausdorff, two proved counterexamples) and the row would be partial under DEC-27; a ruling confirming the literal reading would settle it.
The orientation of w (BBS l.1229–1233) is not pinned: the paper makes no positivity claim. That the axis is actually singular and BBS's degree 2|m| are not asserted by the paper and not formalized.

kb_proposals: To act by ℤ through a homeomorphism φ of M, use GX.HomeoZ φ (Multiplicative ℤ synonym, k • x = (φ ^ k.toInt) x); existsUnique_aeGXQuotient is generic in Γ.

Lifting a real-linear A : ℂ ≃ ℂ to the infinite angle cylinder: rayShift A θ = arg(A e^{iθ}/e^{iθ}) is continuous and in (−π,π) when A has no eigenvalue in (−∞,0] (RayAdmissible); injectivity on DInfty is cplx(2π) plus |Δθ| < 2π (DInfty.eq_of_cplx_eq), which avoids arg-inverse computations.
Determinants of explicit linear maps of ℝ×ℝ×ℝ: GX.det_eq_of_coord (conjugate to Fin 3 → ℝ, Matrix.det_fin_three).

A ℤ-quotient of 𝔻_∞ × Z is Hausdorff only if the action keeps orbits away from the apex in the {r < ε} topology; an action rescaling the Euclidean radius (a boost or null rotation lifted to rays) is not. Act on θ alone (GammaA) and put the Lorentzian geometry in the developing map; check T2 explicitly — existsUnique_aeGXQuotient never needs it.

To build a map equivariant under a homeomorphism F with a fundamental domain [0,T]: GX.exists_equivariant_curve (floor-indexed pieces, LocallyFinite.continuous); to conjugate a turning homeomorphism of ℝ to a translation: GX.exists_turning_curve (strictly monotone on pieces → GX.strictMono_of_strictMonoOn_pieces, surjective by IVT, then StrictMono.orderIsoOfSurjective.toHomeomorph).

Log-polar coordinates of {r>0}: cylPosHomeo with GX.cylPosHomeo_fst / _symm_r / _symm_θ / _symm_snd; conjugating a homeomorphism of the cylinder preserving {r>0} to ℂ × ℝ goes through Homeomorph.subtype (state the iff with `show x ∈ cylPos ℝ ↔ …` to keep the instance-transparency types aligned).
